key_insight: OmegaUse-OfficeVal is a new benchmark designed to test whether LLM agents can complete realistic office-suite workflows over long horizons while staying economically efficient. It adds task-level cost grounding, so performance is judged not just by success, but by how much it costs to get there.
problem_solved: Current LLM agent benchmarks do not adequately evaluate long office-suite task execution or whether agents can do so at a reasonable economic cost. This paper addresses the gap between task completion and practical affordability in real-world office workflows.
method: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a benchmark of 100 office-suite tasks derived from practitioner requests and adapted for evaluation.
Evaluates LLM agents on long-horizon workflows where success depends on completing multi-step office tasks, not just isolated actions.
Incorporates task-level economic grounding to measure the cost-efficiency of agent performance alongside task success.
impact: This benchmark helps researchers and practitioners assess whether LLM agents are actually usable in office settings, where both reliability and cost matter. It can guide the development of more practical, efficient agents for real workplace automation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing a long-horizon office workflow from user request to completed task

paper_title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
paper_authors: Jingbo Zhou, Yusai Zhao, Qi Bao, Jingjia Cao, Zhenghai Chen
